profile.headline: B.S in Electrical & Computer Engineering at CMU | Software Engineer at Qualcomm
profile.summary: Melina Castillo is a junior studying Electrical and Computer Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University. Her main area of interest is hardware design. At CMU, she has taken courses including “Structure and Design of Digital Systems” where she studied and implemented RTL design and computer microarchitecture. Melina completed challenging labs such as implementing Pong entirely on hardware and modifying a simple CPU modeled after RISC-V to create a multiplication operation which was then added to the ISA. Outside of classes, she has taken on the role as a software developer for a startup company she and her colleagues founded called Mycelium. This past summer Melina was a TA for multivariable calculus and an instructor for an intro CS class at the University of Chicago for the Thrive Scholars Summer Academy. Melina is also the president of the Spanish and Latin Student Association, and is a driver on SPIRIT's team for Buggy which is a 100-year-old sport at CMU where students compete in teams to build, push, and race a small, mechanical, torpedo shaped car.

positions.title: Computer Science Instructor & Multivariable Calculus TA
positions.description:

• Manage Canvas pages, host office hours twice a week, and grade tests and assignments for each class

positions.title: Summer Research Intern
positions.description:
• Collected and charted signal data from wireless radio networks across campus using C and Secure Shell 
• Contributed to the Reconfigurable Eco-system for Next-generation End-to-end Wireless (RENEW) project by initiating the implementation of a Python GUI to make data collection more user-friendly

projects.title: A Multiplication Coprocessor for RISC240
projects.description:
Microprocessor microarchitecture
• Wrote assembly code to measure the current performance of multiplication in the RISC240 processor
• Built and tested a multiplication coprocessor to perform the entire algorithm in hardware 
• Optimize the RISC240 microarchitecture and ISA 
• Support two new instructions that perform an 8-bit multiply operation

projects.title: VGA Pong
projects.description:
FPGA hardware thread
• Designed and implemented a hardware thread on an FPGA board to play the Pong video game
• Constructed, tested, and simulated digital combinational and sequential circuits using SystemVerilog and Quartus

organizations.name: SPIRIT Racing Systems (Buggy)
organizations.description:
• Develop mechanical understanding and control of Buggy steering/break system
• Communicate technical feedback with Pusher, Mechanic, and Build teams

organizations.name: Spanish and Latino Student Association
organizations.description:
• Appointed Freshmen Representative (August 2020), elected Internal Relations Chair (April 2021), elected President (April 2022)
• Unify Latine orgs on campus via the Latino and Hispanic Student Leaders Union (LHSLU)
• Oversee the planning of 3-4 large events with 400+ attendees for CMU and larger Pittsburgh area
